subject: Dedicated fit — hardware scenario walkthrough and sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
To: Claire Turner <claire.turner@pegasusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated fit — hardware scenario walkthrough and sizing clarifications

Hi Claire — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and three asks so we can produce a tight Dedicated sizing proposal: 

High-level summary from call:
- Pegasus wants real-time personalization features (recommendations + chat assist) embedded in product pages; SLA target ~95th percentile p99 latency <= 220ms for short chat turn responses (average token output ~60 tokens).
- Expected traffic: steady-state ~120 TPS for inference requests, with 2x daily surge windows (~240 TPS for ~45 minutes).
- Typical prompt shape: user prompt ~40 tokens, system + context ~450 tokens on average; average request = ~500 tokens total (100 input + 400 generation) but token mix varies by endpoint.
- Data residency: US-based VPC preferred, on-prem evaluated for one regulated customer later in FY.

Three clarifying asks (can you confirm by EOD Monday?):
1) Concurrency target: is the 120 TPS the peak sustained (meaning steady concurrent sessions) or an average you expect across endpoints? If "peak sustained," please confirm whether you require headroom (suggested 20% buffer).
2) Token mix: can you share a short sample (or percentiles) of token input vs generated tokens across two routes: (a) short chat (support quick reply) and (b) long form recommendations? A CSV or a handful of examples is fine.
3) GPU preference / constraints: do you have procurement preferences (A100 vs H100) or constraints preventing H100 in your VPC? If unsure, we'll include both options in the sizing workbook.

Attached: pegagus_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx (workbook template for TPS/token scenarios) and sample_latency_profile.csv (toy metrics we use for kernel selection).

Next steps we propose after your confirmations:
- We’ll run the workbook scenarios and return two Dedicated SKU options (cost-optimized + latency-optimized) plus a Hosted fallback design for mixed bursts.
- Schedule a 45-minute ops walkthrough next week with your infra lead to validate VPC & KMS details.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your token-sample + confirmation on concurrency & GPU preference.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com | +1 415-555-0196
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Turner <claire.turner@pegasusai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
Cc: ops@pegasusai.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated fit — hardware scenario walkthrough and sizing clarifications

Thanks Naomi — great recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) Concurrency / TPS: the 120 TPS is our expected steady-state peak for the primary recommendation endpoint (we've modelled it as sustained during business hours). We want a 25% buffer for safety during marketing spikes — so please size for 150 TPS sustained with the ability to absorb 240 TPS burst.

2) Token mix: attaching a small sample (ops included) — percentiles below for the two routes you asked about: 
- Short chat (support quick reply): 50th input: 30 tokens, 95th input: 80 tokens; generation median: 40 tokens, 95th: 120 tokens.
- Recommendations (longer context): 50th input: 120 tokens, generation median: 350 tokens, 95th gen: 900 tokens (rare).

3) GPU preference: ops prefers H100 if available because we have internal benchmarks on cost-per-token with quantization. They can provision H100 in our US VPC but need cost delta shown. If H100 isn't possible for the POC, A100 is acceptable.

Attachments: sample_token_profile.csv (attached here). We'll ask infra to be on the ops walkthrough next week; propose Wed 12/09 at 10am PT.

Claire
Claire Turner | Head of Product, Pegasus AI
claire.turner@pegasusai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Claire Turner <claire.turner@pegasusai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated fit — hardware scenario walkthrough and sizing clarifications

Appreciate the quick answers Claire — that helps a lot. A few notes from a sizing / ops perspective: 

- We will produce two SKU families in the workbook: one H100-centric (latency-optimized) and one A100-centric (cost-optimized). For the H100 path we'll assume aggressive quantization (4-bit where safe) and GPU-side KV caching.
- For 150 sustained TPS and 240 TPS bursts (short windows), initial recommendation: 6 x H100-80GB or equivalent (with continuous batching and prefix/KV caching) should meet p95/p99 latency targets for short chat flows — we'll validate with microbenchmarks. If A100-only, expect ~8-10 x A100-80GB depending on efficiency.
- Concurrency model: we'll design for 120-160 concurrent active contexts per GPU (depends on sequence length and KV memory). We'll include guidance on per-GPU concurrency, batch sizes, and autoscale thresholds that trigger burst capacity (hosted fallback) to avoid cold degradations.

Ben will run a microbenchmarking pass once Naomi fills the workbook with the CSV token samples you provided. Naomi: happy to lead the benchmarks next Wed after the ops walkthrough.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: scheduling + POC scope (Pegasus)

Internal note — copying into the thread for record (not sent to Pegasus yet).

POC scope (proposal):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week benchmark + 2-week integration/validation)
- Targets: Validate p95/p99 latency under 150 TPS sustained + 240 TPS burst for short chat route; validate token-cost delta H100 vs A100 for recommendation route (long-form).
- Deliverables: microbenchmark results, cost-projection workbook, recommended Dedicated SKU + Hosted fallback runbook, ops-ready deployment checklist (VPC/KMS/DNS).

Action items:
- Naomi: finalize workbook with Claire's sample_token_profile.csv and share by Mon 12/08 EOD (required for Ben to run benchmarks).
- Ben: plan benchmarking harness and required model variants; target Wed 12/09 for the ops walkthrough and start of microbench.
- Marissa: draft commercial term options (3/6/12 month committed tiers) after we have modelled cost numbers.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodai.com>
To: Claire Turner <claire.turner@pegasusai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated fit — hardware scenario walkthrough and sizing clarifications

Thanks all — Claire, workbook with your sample_token_profile.csv is attached (pegasus_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx). I populated three traffic scenarios: baseline (120 TPS), buffer (150 TPS sustained), and burst (240 TPS spikes). Key assumptions are noted in the top worksheet. 

Quick summary of what we’ll run Wed after the ops walkthrough:
- Microbench: H100 (4-bit quant) + A100 (8-bit mixed) across short chat and recommendations model variants; measure p95/p99 and memory footprint.
- Autoscale: simulate steady 150 TPS plus a 45-minute burst to validate scale-up time and fallback to Hosted API for the highest peaks.
- Cost model: per-token and per-hour comparisons for both GPU families and expected committed tiers.

Claire — confirming Wed 12/09 10am PT for ops walkthrough. I’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in and pre-reads.

—Naomi
